What does carpet installation cost in Lynnwood, WA?

Figure $4 to $7 per square foot installed in Lynnwood — that covers carpet, pad, labor, new tack strip and hauling the old carpet away. Most projects total $2,000 to $4,500; a 1,200 sq ft main floor plus a staircase generally comes in at $5,500 to $8,500. The grade of carpet you choose moves the price most, and you choose it at home from the samples in our van.
Does the mobile carpet showroom really come to Lynnwood?

It does — the van works Lynnwood every week. It carries 20+ carpet samples and all three pad grades, and we unroll them in the room you're carpeting so you judge color in your own light instead of a store's. While we're there we measure every room and stair, and you keep a written price from that same visit. The trip costs you nothing.
What does carpet stretching cost in Lynnwood?

Stretching starts at $99 per room in Lynnwood. We hook up a power stretcher, pull out the ripples and loose spots, and re-secure the edges — typically about a fifth of what replacing the same carpet would run. If the pile still stands up and the color still works for you, stretching is usually the smarter spend.
What is the per-step price to carpet stairs in Lynnwood?

Stair installation starts at $18 per step, in either a waterfall wrap or a tailored cap-and-band look. Landings and pie-shaped winder steps are measured and written into the quote at the start, so the stair total you approve is the stair total you pay.
How long does a Lynnwood carpet install take?

One day, for most Lynnwood homes. A crew comfortably handles three or four rooms and a staircase between morning and evening; a full house with heavy furniture can stretch into a second day. The schedule is written on your quote, so you know before install day, not during it.
Do the installers move my furniture, or is that on me?

We move the big pieces — beds, dressers, sofas, tables — and set them back in place once the carpet is in; that's included on most jobs. What we ask you to handle is the small stuff: closet floors, electronics, breakables, and anything personal you'd rather box up yourself.
Is it smarter to stretch my carpet or put in new?

If the pile stands back up, the backing is sound and the color still suits the room, a $99-per-room stretch buys you years. New carpet is the right call when traffic lanes are worn flat, seams are pulling apart, the backing is breaking down, or pet odor has outlived a professional cleaning. We look first and tell you which job you actually have.
Which parts of Lynnwood does OC Flooring cover?

All of them — Alderwood Manor, City Center, South Lynnwood, Scriber Lake, Cedar Valley, College Place, Meadowdale, Perrinville, Martha Lake, Lake Serene, Swamp Creek and Picnic Point — plus Mountlake Terrace, Brier, Edmonds, Mill Creek and the rest of south Snohomish County.
What carpet holds up best with dogs and cats?

Solution-dyed nylon over a moisture-barrier pad. The color runs through the fiber, so it takes hard cleaning — even diluted bleach — without fading, and the barrier pad plus a sealed backing keep accidents from soaking into the subfloor, which is where odor becomes permanent. The barrier pad upgrade starts at $0.65 per square foot.
What warranty comes with a Lynnwood carpet install?

Two layers. OC Flooring covers the workmanship — seams, stretch, transitions — with a 1-year warranty, and the mill covers the carpet itself, usually 10 to 25 years on wear and stain depending on grade. Both are spelled out on your written quote. Worth knowing: some mill warranties require a specific pad grade, which is one more reason all three grades come to the measure.
